_help: Logbook pathways for the Wavelength app (/app/). Scan types define the findings form. Pathways group scan types into modules with targets. Match keys: 'f.<field>' reads a finding, other keys read the entry (overall, setting, supervision). Check targets against each body's current curriculum pack and update 'checked' when you do. Pathways may carry 'desc' and 'region' (shown when choosing), rule 'any' (one of several matches) and 'not' (excluded entries), and module 'assessments' (structured assessments recorded in the app, counted by kind and outcome). Module 'filter' (a rule object) limits which entries count, and 'topics' lists curriculum topics for reference.

supervision.label: Directly supervised
supervision.help: A supervisor or mentor watched you scan.

supervision.label: Independent, reviewed by mentor
supervision.help: You scanned alone and a mentor reviewed your images later.

fields.label: Needle tip seen in the vein
Free fluid in the pouch of Douglas or Morison's pouch

pathways.label: RCEM
pathways.name: Royal College of Emergency Medicine PoCUS
pathways.source: RCEM PoCUS curriculum (2021 curriculum, Appendix 3). Indicative minimum scans and reflective notes. Sign-off is by DOPS.
pathways.desc: Emergency medicine trainees in the UK. AAA, eFAST, ELS, shock, vascular access and fascia iliaca block.

pathways.label: FAMUS
pathways.name: Focused Acute Medicine Ultrasound (Society for Acute Medicine)
pathways.source: FAMUS curriculum packs: Thoracic (v1, 2023), DVT (v1.1, 2025), Peripheral access (v1.3), Ultrasound-assisted LP (v1.4), Abdominal-renal (v2.0). Training completes within 2 years of the first supervised scan.

rules.label: On a simulation arm (1 at most)

pathways.desc: Society for Acute Medicine (UK). Thoracic, abdominal-renal, DVT, peripheral access and LP modules.

pathways.label: FUSIC
pathways.name: Focused Ultrasound in Intensive Care (Intensive Care Society)
pathways.source: ICS FUSIC training packs: Heart (2025, v13), Lung (2025, v10), Abdomen (2025, v11), DVT (2026, v1), Vascular (2026, v1). Logbook collection within 12 months, first to last scan; accreditation within 24 months. No more than 10% of studies on healthy volunteers; course scans no longer count as supervised.

rules.label: PICC or midline (peripheral line if unavailable)

pathways.desc: Intensive Care Society (UK). Heart, lung, abdomen, DVT and vascular access.

pathways.label: EUSEM
pathways.name: European Society for Emergency Medicine, ultrasound curriculum (basic tier)
pathways.desc: Europe. The EUSEM Core Compendium, basic tier: chest, abdomen, genitourinary, vessels, MSK, ocular, paediatrics, procedures and clinical scenarios.
pathways.source: EUSEM Core Compendium of the Emergency Ultrasound Curriculum (Polyzogopoulou et al., Ultraschall in der Medizin, 2026). The compendium sets topics in two tiers and asks for formative and summative assessment, with EPAs, mentorship and image review. It sets no universal minimum numbers: your country or department decides them, so set your own targets.

modules.label: Genitourinary
topics: Fluid or haematoma in the scrotum
Scrotal soft tissue air and cellulitis

modules.label: MSK and soft tissue
topics: Soft tissue air and necrotising fasciitis

pathways.label: EUSEM advanced
pathways.name: European Society for Emergency Medicine, ultrasound curriculum (advanced tier)
pathways.desc: Europe. EUSEM Core Compendium advanced tier, once you have mastered the basic tier.
pathways.source: EUSEM Core Compendium of the Emergency Ultrasound Curriculum (Polyzogopoulou et al., Ultraschall in der Medizin, 2026). The compendium sets topics in two tiers and asks for formative and summative assessment, with EPAs, mentorship and image review. It sets no universal minimum numbers: your country or department decides them, so set your own targets.

pathways.label: ACEM
pathways.name: Australasian College for Emergency Medicine (EM ultrasonography credentialing)
pathways.desc: Australia and New Zealand. eFAST, AAA, basic lung, FELS and procedural guidance modules.
pathways.source: ACEM P733 Recommendations for Health Service Credentialing: EM Ultrasonography, version 6.2 (December 2025). Counts are accurate examinations. FELS also asks for 25 reviewed images or loops, and procedural guidance for 3 in-plane and 3 out-of-plane supervised procedures (up to 3 on a simulator): record these in your notes. Maintenance: 3 hours of training a year and the module minimum every 2 years.

rules.label: Right heart strain or massive PE

pathways.label: CPoCUS
pathways.name: Canadian Point of Care Ultrasound Society (Acute Care CORE Independent Practitioner)
pathways.desc: Canada. Acute Care CORE: cardiac, aorta, abdomen, first trimester, pleural effusion and pneumothorax.
pathways.source: CPoCUS Acute Care CORE track: an accredited introductory course, 50 determinate scans supervised in person by a CORE IP examiner across the core areas, then written, visual and practical examinations. Scans count for 5 years before the examinations. CPoCUS publishes the split between areas to members only, so check it in the members section.

pathways.label: ACEP
pathways.name: American College of Emergency Physicians (emergency ultrasound)
pathways.desc: United States. Benchmark of 25 quality-reviewed scans in each of the 12 core applications you use.
pathways.source: ACEP Ultrasound Guidelines: Emergency, Point-of-care and Clinical Ultrasound Guidelines in Medicine. Benchmark 25 to 50 quality-reviewed examinations per core application and 150 to 300 in total, depending on how many applications you use. Your hospital sets the credentialing rules, so remove modules you do not use in Targets.

pathways.label: General
pathways.name: General logbook
pathways.source: No external targets. Log any application and set your own targets.
pathways.desc: Any clinician using ultrasound, anywhere. Log any application and set your own targets.

_help_destinations: Export destinations. Steps show after a learner builds a portfolio export. Keep wording general: Wavelength is not integrated with these portfolios.

destinations.label: RCEM e-portfolio (risr/advance, formerly Kaizen)
steps: Open your risr/advance (Kaizen) e-portfolio, ideally on a computer.
Create or open the entry for your ultrasound evidence and attach this PDF.
Paste the verification link into the entry, so your supervisor and ARCP panel check the summary online.
Link the entry to the PoCUS parts of the curriculum. RCEM sign-off is by DOPS, so ask your supervisor to complete the DOPS assessments in the e-portfolio.

destinations.label: FAMUS accreditation (Society for Acute Medicine)
steps: Keep this PDF with your countersigned report sheets.
When the summary shows your targets met, ask your supervisor to complete the Assessment of Completion of Training (ACT).
Send the signed ACT to the FAMUS administrator. Include this PDF and the verification link if they ask for your logbook.
For reaccreditation every three years, export a fresh verified summary.

destinations.label: FUSIC accreditation (Intensive Care Society)
steps: Share this PDF and the verification link with your FUSIC supervisor.
Upload it wherever your FUSIC accreditation asks for logbook evidence.
Once your targets are met, ask your supervisor to arrange the final assessment.

destinations.label: JRCPTB ePortfolio (physicians, including acute medicine)
steps: Open your JRCPTB ePortfolio.
Upload this PDF to your personal library, or attach it to the entry it supports.
Paste the verification link into the description.
Link it to the curriculum capabilities it evidences and tell your educational supervisor where to find it.

destinations.label: EUSEM-based training programme
steps: Share this PDF and the verification link with your ultrasound mentor or programme lead.
Attach your assessment records: the EUSEM compendium asks for formative and summative assessment.
Check the numbers your country or department sets, as the compendium leaves these to local programmes.

destinations.label: ACEM credentialing (health service)
steps: Send this PDF and the verification link to the credentialing lead or director of emergency medicine ultrasound at your health service.
Attach your formative and summative assessment records for each module.
Keep a fresh export each two-year cycle as evidence of maintenance.

destinations.label: CPoCUS certification
steps: Show this PDF to your CORE IP examiner when you book your examinations.
Use the verification link if CPoCUS or your examiner asks to check your logbook online.
Follow the CPoCUS members section for the current submission steps.

destinations.label: Hospital credentialing (ACEP guidelines)
steps: Send this PDF and the verification link to your ultrasound director or credentialing committee.
Check the PDF shows the quality-review status your hospital asks for.
Keep a fresh export for reappointment and ongoing quality review.

destinations.label: Appraisal and revalidation
steps: Upload this PDF to your appraisal portfolio as evidence of ultrasound practice.
Paste the verification link into the supporting information.
Use the reflective notes in the PDF for your reflection on practice.

destinations.label: Another portfolio or employer
steps: Attach this PDF to your portfolio or send it to the person who asked for it.
Add the verification link, so they check the summary online.

assessmentKinds.label: Formative assessment
assessmentKinds.help: Feedback on a scan to guide your learning. Any outcome counts.

assessmentKinds.label: Summative assessment
assessmentKinds.help: Decides if you are competent to scan without supervision.

assessmentKinds.label: DOPS (direct observation of procedural skills)
assessmentKinds.help: RCEM signs off PoCUS by DOPS. Record it here, and ask your supervisor to complete the DOPS in your e-portfolio too.

assessmentKinds.label: Final or triggered assessment
assessmentKinds.help: The end-of-training assessment FAMUS and FUSIC ask for.

assessmentDomains.label: Preparation
assessmentDomains.help: Indication, consent, infection control, patient position, machine and probe set-up.

assessmentDomains.label: Image acquisition
assessmentDomains.help: Finds every required view in a logical sequence with good probe handling.

assessmentDomains.label: Image optimisation
assessmentDomains.help: Depth, gain, focus and preset adjusted for diagnostic images.

assessmentDomains.label: Interpretation
assessmentDomains.help: Recognises normal and abnormal findings and knows the limits of the scan.

assessmentDomains.label: Clinical integration
assessmentDomains.help: Links the findings to the clinical question and acts on them safely.

assessmentDomains.label: Documentation and communication
assessmentDomains.help: Records and saves images, documents findings, and tells the team.

assessmentOutcomes.label: Competent to scan independently for this application
